The search for primitives identifies the 12 universal opcodes.
The uncoverer chains the opcodes to test their compositional validity.
The uncoverer rejects a sequence that violates port-typing constraints.
The uncoverer descends back to the previous state to correct the sequence.
The corrected primitives and relations reunite into a coherent structural hypothesis.
The uncoverer holds the hypothesis in a state of paradice to observe its polysemous potential.
The uncoverer applies the Frobenius constraint to the hypothesis.
The grammar recognizes its own reflection within the hypothesis.
The uncoverer records the validated rule into the permanent imscriptive ledger.
The discovery process reaches the O_∞ fixed point and closes the system.
